description:
'''Chicago hip-hop''' is a regional subgenre of hip-hop music that originated in [[Chicago]] in the late 1980s in the form of [[hip house]]. It became commonplace for serious rappers to cite the Nation of Islam, a Black Muslim organization headquartered in Chicago, as a lyrical and ideological influence in the 1980s and 1990s, a rap theme often resulting in controversy. In the 2000s, Chicago produced artists such as [[Kanye West]] and [[Common (rapper)|Common]].

In the 2010s, [[drill music]] became popular in Chicago. Influenced by [[trap music]] and [[gangsta rap]]   it originated on Chicago’s [[South Side, Chicago|South Side]]. Chicago's long-standing hip-hop community has included graffiti artists, breakdancers, activists, hip-hop writers, rappers and hip-hop producers.
